headline: Exporting the same three modules as JSX components instead of style values costs every lane, hand-written vanilla included, and costs next-yak its fold outright: a styled component cannot be folded across a module boundary.

microbench.why: The declarations, the three modules and the rendered element are identical to the Example `button-variants` shown above; only the API changes. Every lane pays for that. `vanilla` falls from 1.78M to 1.35M renders/s purely for the two extra React components in the tree, which prices an unfoldable component API before any library is involved. `next-yak` falls further, from 2.23M to 1.28M, because `styled(Button)` declared in another module leaves `fold_jsx_usages` nothing to rewrite, and it ends up level with its own `foldStatic: false` lane at 1.25M. The atomic lanes give up least, `stylex` from 1.27M to 1.02M, since they were already merging at render.

autocannon.why: `next-yak` at 1,146 req/s, `next-yak-nofold` at 1,018 and `vanilla` at 1,012 finish inside 13% of each other, which is the shape of a case where nobody folds. `styled-components` at 676 req/s fares relatively better here than on the value form, since a component API is the shape it was designed around.

attribution.why: `vanilla` posts the lowest total at 0.803 ms, with 0.285 ms of component self-time for the three nested functions and no library at all. `next-yak` needs 0.881 ms, 0.381 ms of it lib self-time inside the `Yak` wrappers folding would have removed, and `next-yak-nofold` records 0.361 ms in that same slice, which confirms nothing folded. `emotion` at 2.94 ms and `goober` at 2.00 ms stay dominated by their serializers.

hydrate.why: Bimodal, like its sibling case: `next-yak` reads 88.5 ms here and 46.5 ms in the previous battery, with samples between 44.1 ms and 93.8 ms. The ordering inside the leading group is noise. `next-yak-nofold` at 46.1 ms, `panda` at 47.3 ms and `bamboo` at 47.8 ms are the modes that recur.

inp.why: Eleven lanes answer a single click between 7.0 ms and 8.0 ms, indistinguishable at this spread. Only `goober` at 11.1 ms and `emotion` at 10.6 ms separate from the group.

mount.why: Cold mount compresses eleven lanes into 71.5 ms through 88.0 ms, with `next-yak` at 71.5 ms and `next-yak-nofold` at 73.1 ms tied inside their spreads — and `next-yak` no longer has the 25 ms mount it posts on the value form, because there is a component chain to construct here. Extra fibers cost render time, and layout is what dominates a mount.

renderTiming.why: One style recalculation per lane, costing 0.134 ms to 0.182 ms. The API shape changes what React does, not what the style engine has to match.

payload.why: `vanilla` ships 3,164 gz B with no JS. `next-yak` ships 4,078 B, which is 189 B more than the same ladder written as style values, because the component form keeps three wrappers instead of one folded class. The runtime libraries are unchanged from the value form, 13.5 kB of JS for `styled-components` and 13.0 kB for `emotion`, since what they ship is the library rather than the ladder.

nsweep.why: `next-yak` at 3.02 ms and `next-yak-nofold` at 3.14 ms trace the same line, which states the case as plainly as it can be stated: folding that cannot cross a module boundary is worth nothing at any size. `vanilla` at 3.13 ms sits with them, `emotion` at 10.8 ms sets the far end.

crossCase: This is the Example `button-variants` shown above with each module exporting a JSX component instead of a style value, so the pair prices the API shape rather than the file layout — both are split three ways. The same asymmetry runs through the Example `multifile-shop`: exported values fold across a boundary, exported components do not. The css-prop lanes have no cell here at all, because the css prop cannot take a style fragment as a component prop and the case does not compile for them, which is a limitation worth knowing before choosing that API.
